title: Days Past Due at Which an Auto Loan Changes Standing
content:
Two thresholds, both counted in days past due, mark the points at which a loan of the Auto Loans line changes standing in the bank's records.

| Threshold | Used Vehicle Loan | Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle Loan | Auto Refinance Loan | Lease Buyout Loan | New Vehicle Loan | Green Vehicle Loan |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Days past due at which the loan becomes delinquent | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Days past due at which the remaining principal is charged off | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 |

Both thresholds read the same on every product of the Auto Loans line, so a borrower's product never changes the day on which either point is reached; only the day count on the loan does.

## The two thresholds side by side

A loan 29 days past due has reached neither threshold. A loan 30 days past due has reached the first. A loan 119 days past due has reached the first and not the second. A loan 120 days past due has reached both.
